questions.question: What is "NIKKEI"?

options.text: Share Price Index of Tokyo Share Market
The Japanese name of country’s Planning Commission

questions.solution:
NIKKEI is the Share Price Index of Tokyo Share Market.

 
• It is also known as Nikkei 225, the Nikkei index, or the Nikkei Stock Average.
 
• It is a stock market index for the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).
 
• Nihon Keizai Shinbun (Nikkei Inc’s flagship publication) newspaper is calculating the Nikkei Index since 1950.

questions.question: Which ﬁve year plan aimed at following regional approach, instead of a sectoral approach so as to bring down regional inequalities?
questions.solution:
The Tenth Five Year Plan aimed at following regional approach, instead of a sectoral approach so as to bring down regional inequalities.

 
• The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-2007) was launched on December 21, 2002 by the then PM, Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
 
• Major objectives of this plan were:
 
 
• Target of 8% GDP growth.
 
• To increase literacy rates up to 75 %.
 
• 50 million new jobs in the non-farm, non-industrial sector.
 
• To reduce poverty by 5 percent.
 
• To provide all the villages, an access to drinking water.
 
• Cleaning of major polluted rivers by 2007.

questions.question: Saint Ramananda associated with which of the following branches?
questions.solution:
Saint Ramananda is associated with Ram Magri.

 
• Ram Magri or Ram Bhakti was a Rama-oriented movement, which focussed on meditation of Sri Ramchandra.
 
• Ramananda (14th century) was the chief pioneer of Ram Bhakti.
 
• For the most part of his life, he lived in Varanasi.
 
• Born in a Brahmin family, he was a devotional poet.
 
• His disciples include Saint Kabir, Guru Ravidas and others.

questions.question: Who of the following leaders is NOT associated with Champaran Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
Sardar Patel is NOT associated with Champaran Satyagraha.

 
• During the British Raj, the Champaran Satyagraha started in 1917 in the district of Bihar.
 
• It was launched by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The European planters at Champaran in Bihar practised indigo cultivation through illegal methods and forced the Indian farmers to cultivate Indigo on 3/20th part of their land. This was called Tinkathia system.
 
• This natural Indigo was used to make dye. The Germans, by then, had invented the way to make artificial dye because of which the demand for natural Indigo fell.
 
• Now, if the farmers wished to shift to cultivate other crops, they could do so only by paying large amount of ‘compensation’ or ‘tawan’.
 
• Thus, Champaran’s peasants with the help of Gandhi Ji and Rajendra Prasad organized Champaran Satyagraha and abolished Tinkathia system (1919).

questions.question: Whose science is Seismography?
questions.solution:
Seismography is the science of Earthquake.

 
• Seismography is recording and measuring the vibrations produced by the earthquake.
 
• The instrument which is used to measure such vibrations is called a seismometer.

questions.question: What is called the small grasslands on the slopes of Lesser Himalayan range in Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The small grasslands on the slopes of Lesser Himalayan range in Jammu and Kashmir are called Marg.

 
• The extension of Lesser Himalaya lies in the south of Great Himalayas. It is 80 to 100 km wide and its average height is between 2700 km to 4500 km.
 
• Pir Panjal Range and Dhuladhar Range are several small ranges under the lesser Himalayas.
 
• There are small meadows in the slopes of lesser Himalayas. These are known as marg in Kashmir (Gulmarg (Meadow of Flowers), SoneMarg) etc.

questions.question: Folk dance "Lai Haraoba" is popular in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Folk dance "Lai Haraoba" is popular in Manipur.

 
• Associated with the Meitei People (an ethnic group of Manipur), Lai Haraoba, is a festival celebrated to please Sanamahism (a traditional deity).
 
• It is celebrated to honor the Sylvan deities known as Umang Lai.
 
• The festival represents the worship of traditional deities and ancestors.

questions.question: Which countries organized joint military exercise named ‘Mitra Shakti’ in October 2017?
questions.solution:
India – Srilanka organized joint military exercise named ‘Mitra Shakti’ in October 2017.

 
• It was held in Aundh Military Station in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• The series of Mitra Shakti exercise between Sri Lanka and India had started in 2012 as a reaction to China’s efforts to increase its impact in the Indian Ocean region and South Asia.
 
• The goal of this exercise is to form a strong military-to-military bond between the two nation’s armies.

questions.question:
Generally covalently bonded molecules ________.

I. Have high boiling and melting point as compared to ionically bonded molecules

II. Are poor conductors of electricity.

III. Have weak inter-molecular force.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covalent Bond:**

 
 
• **A type of chemical bond wherein two or more atoms share one or more electron pairs.**
 
• The outer shell of each has crossed over the other,
 
• Each atom shares its valence electron with the other atom.
 
• It can be said as an electrostatic force of attraction between two or more atoms or molecules.
 
• There are two types of covalent bonds - sigma and pi bonds.
 
• Sigma is the strongest covalent bond while pi-bond is the weakest covalent bond.
 
 
 
• Sigma and Pi bonds:-
 
 
• The overlapping of atomic orbitals distinguishes the **sigma and pi bonds from each other.**
 
• The overlapping of atomic orbitals forms covalent bonds.
 
• The head-to-head overlapping of atomic orbitals forms sigma bonds, whereas the lateral overlap of two atomic orbitals forms pi bonds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Covalently bonded compounds do not have free electrons, so they do not conduct electric current.​ 
 
• Covalently bonded molecules have low melting and boiling points because intermolecular forces are weak and little amount of energy is required to break the forces.
 
• If the compounds have high melting and boiling point then they have very strong or strong intermolecular forces. 
 
• If compounds have medium melting and boiling point then they have medium intermolecular forces.
 
• The intermolecular forces between water molecules are stronger than those between oxygen molecules.
 
• Covalent bonds are formed by the mutual sharing of electrons.
 
• Hence the covalently bonded molecules have strong bonds within the molecule.

questions.question: Who summons the joint sitting of both the houses of the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**2**__ i.e __**President of India**__.

__
 
• According to Article 108 of the Indian constitution, the joint sitting of the Parliament is called by the President__.
 
• It is presided over by the Speaker or, in his absence, by the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha or in his absence, the Deputy-Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Joint session of Parliament can be summoned in the following situations -
 
 
• If after a Bill has been passed by one House and submitted to the other House and the Bill is rejected by the other House.
 
• The Houses have finally disagreed as to the amendments to be made in the Bill.
 
• More than six months elapse from the date of the reception of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it.
 
 
 
• The President may, unless the Bill has elapsed by reason of a dissolution of the House of the People, notify to the Houses by message if they are sitting or by public notification if they are not sitting, his intention to summon them to meet in a joint sitting for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill.

questions.question: Which bill can be introduced without the prior recommendation of the President of India?
questions.solution:
Ordinary Bill can be introduced without the prior recommendation of the President of India.

 
• Features of an Ordinary bill:
 
 
• It can be introduced in either house of Parliament.
 
• It can be introduced by both Minister and a private member, unlike Money bills which can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha by a Minister.
 
• Unlike other bills, it can be accepted, rejected or returned by the President for reconsideration.

questions.question: Where does glucose break down into pyruvate?
questions.solution:
• Glucose breaks down into pyruvate in Cytoplasm.
 
• The process of conversion of glucose into pyruvate releasing ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is called Glycolysis.
 
• When the pyruvate enters the mitochondria, it is converted into carbon dioxide and water.

questions.question: In December 2017, the Prime Minister of India inaugurated the B. R. Ambedkar International Centre in ________.
questions.solution:
In December 2017, the Prime Minister of India inaugurated the B. R. Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi.

 
• It is an important center for research on economic and social issues.
 
• It will promote the thoughts and teachings of B.R Ambedkar.
 
• Popularly known as Babasaheb Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (1891 - 1956) was an Indian economist, jurist, politician and social reformer.
 
• He campaigned against the discrimination towards Dalits (the Untouchables).

questions.question: Who expanded the cell theory and suggested that all the cells arise from pre-existing cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudolf Virchow**__ .

Rudolf Virchow expanded the cell theory and suggested that all the cells arise from pre-existing cells.

 
• The cell theory, given by Rudolf Virchow in 1855, states that:
 
 
• All living organisms are made up of cells.
 
• The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
 
• All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Which enzyme has been used by scientists of Massachusetts Institute of Technology to induce plants to give off the dim light?
questions.solution:
Luciferase enzyme has been used by scientists of Massachusetts Institute of Technology (in 2017) to induce plants to give off a dim light.

 
• The objective of this experiment was to make the plant work as a desk lamp which is not powered by electricity.

questions.question: On 29 September 2017, SEBI allowed Sovereign wealth fund and other long term Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to buy corporate debt up to _________ in infrastructure sector.
questions.solution:
On 29 September 2017, SEBI allowed Sovereign wealth fund and other long term Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to buy corporate debt up to Rs 9500 crore in infrastructure sector.

 
• SEBI stands for - The Securities and Exchange Board of India.
 
• The move was executed after RBI’s decision to keep out foreign investment in popularly known masala bonds (the rupee dominated bonds) from the Combined Corporate Debt Limit (CCDL).

questions.question: On 2 January 2018, Parliament Passed NABARD (Amendment) Bill, 2017. The Bill seeks to increase the capital of NABARD from Rs 5,000 crore to ______.
questions.solution:
On 2 January 2018, Parliament Passed NABARD (Amendment) Bill, 2017. The Bill seeks to increase the capital of NABARD from Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 30,000 crore.

 
• NABARD stands for - National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.
 
• The responsibility to regulate facilities like credit for industrial and agricultural development in the rural areas.
 
• To amend the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981, is the aim of this bill.

questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) produced in a body of mass 10 kg when a force of 20 N is applied on it
questions.solution:
The acceleration (in m/s2) produced in a body of mass 10 kg when a force of 20 N is applied on it is 2 m/s².

 
• The formula for force: force = mass × acceleration.
 
• Therefore acceleration = force ÷ mass.
 
• Here acceleration = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 m/s².

questions.question: The product of mass of a body and the acceleration produced in it equals the _________ acting on it.
questions.solution:
The product of the mass of a body and the acceleration produced in it equals the Force acting on it.

__CONCEPT:__

 
• Force: It is those physical quantities that are defined as the push or pull of an object.

 
 
• Its unit is Newton.
 
 

Equation of Force:

⇒ F = ma

Where m is the mass and a is the acceleration of the body

questions.question: The process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the earth is called ________.
questions.solution:
The process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the earth is called Earthing.

__
 
• Importance of Earthing:
 
 
• It protects human lives by providing safety to electrical appliances from leakage of current.
 
• It protects buildings form lighting.
 
• It removes the risk of fire in electrical systems.
 
 

Explanation:__

There are two types of charges found in nature -

 
• Positive charge
 
• Negative charge

Properties of charges:

 
• Like charges (same charges) repel each other.
 
• Unlike charges (different charges) attract each other.
 
• When two objects are rubbed against each other, they develop charges.
 
• Earthing: The process of transfer of charge from a charged object to the Earth is known as Earthing.
 
• Lightning is caused because of the build-up of electrostatic charges in the clouds.
 
• Lightning Conductor: It is a device used to protect buildings from the effect of lightning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/925f01df4e3ec65250564381709186f9ad472eb76c3f879f6b9cc978e01e0109.png] 

 
• A metallic rod, taller than the building, is installed in the walls of the building during its construction.
 
• One end of the rod is kept out in the air and the other is buried deep in the ground.
 
• The rod provides an easy route for the transfer of electric charge to the ground.
 
• Copper is used because it is a good conductor of electricity.
 
• The lightning conductor is sharp-pointed because this will ensure a high electric field and hence the quick flow of electric charges to the ground.

questions.question: The overall capabilities of CCT are understood by all because _________ are information processing tools.
questions.solution:
The overall capabilities of CCT are understood by all because Computers are information processing tools.

 
• CCT stands for - Computers and Communication Technology.
 
• The socio-economic divides in our society are balanced by CCT as it gives an access to those who were deprived of relevant information.
